claim: For Component Intelligence v0.1, the most important choice is how a verdict gets computed. The storage format (graph, typed records or rules) matters less. The system should list every obligation an assembly must meet, derived from component types, and grade each one. It should not just collect whatever defects its detectors happen to find. A pairwise compatibility-rule engine running over an interface graph cannot see a relationship that is missing. If a rotating shaft has no shaft_to_bearing edge, no rule fires, no finding appears, and the result defaults to PASS. Every validator and graph pattern OMNI uses today has that default-pass shape. The one relationship graph OMNI already has (mission_graph) goes further: it fills missing links with a keyword match or the first available target, and it does this before its coverage checks run. An implementation that follows these existing patterns would therefore miss the mission's structural failures, even with the value-level KNOWN/UNKNOWN and provenance typing proposed in OMNI-FRONTIER-0002. The missed cases would be an unsupported rotating shaft, a belt drive with no tensioning, a leadscrew with no fixed/floating support, and a bearing with no axial retention. Prediction: v0.1 fails closed on structural omissions only if (a) component types and pattern roles declare required ports with cardinality, alternative ways to satisfy them, and provenance; (b) a closure step turns every required port in the assembly into an obligation before any compatibility rule runs; (c) the overall verdict is the worst verdict across that obligation set, and an empty or partially covered set can never be PASS; and (d) CAD obligations come only from bound interfaces, so an unbound port produces a finding and no geometry.
mechanism:
KNOWN FACTS (from reading the repo):

(1) Default-pass aggregation is the standard pattern in the repo. workshop_part_validator.py:59-64, validation_engine.py:177-181 and knowledge_gate_validator.py:354-358 all start at "pass"/"passed" and only move down when a check adds a warning or blocker. rover_calculators.py:69 also starts at "PASS". With no applicable detector, the result is PASS.

(2) The existing relationship graph builds links from text similarity. mission_graph/enrichment.py:59-62 links a component to a data bus when bus.protocol is a substring of comp.interface. Lines 67-77 link ROS2 nodes to components when any word of 4 or more characters overlaps. The mission explicitly forbids treating semantic similarity as compatibility.

(3) The graph invents links to fill gaps. enrichment.py:99-116 sets any component or CAD feature that has no body_region_id to region_ids[0]. builder.py:482-484 runs enrich_graph before check_graph. reviewer.py:83-90 raises COMP_MISSING_BODY_REGION only when body_region_id is empty. So once any region exists, the missing-relationship warning can no longer fire: a missing relationship has been replaced by a made-up one.

(4) Coverage obligations are the same for every component regardless of type. reviewer.py:68-90 checks power rail, data bus and body region on every component, and missing links are only ever severity "warning". Nothing can say that a rotating shaft must have radial support (FAIL) while a passive plate needs no power rail.

(5) An empty graph gets a clean review. tests/test_mission_graph_phase6_review.py:204-205 asserts that review_graph on an empty graph returns issues == [].

(6) OMNI has one partial precedent for enumerating required items. golden_standard_validator.py:150-170 lists required artifacts, calculations and checks and counts the missing ones. But status "passed" only needs score >= 0.90, so up to 10% of required items can be missing and still pass. An empty requirement list gives 0.0 → "failed", which is fail-closed. reliability/gates.py:38-39 returns BLOCKED for an empty gate list. The rover calculation gate (reliability_service.py:659-664) turns missing required calculations into WARN, not UNKNOWN or BLOCKED.

(7) The CAD IR has no relationship concept. SubassemblySpec (cad_assembly_ir.py:248-270) holds flat lists of components, mounting features and fastener patterns. MechanicalComponentSpec (194-226) has no ports or interfaces. mechanical_component_library.py describes attachment only as a free-text mounting_hint.

WHY THIS MATTERS (inference): The mission's examples fall into two kinds. Value defects (bore ≠ seat diameter; speed rating unavailable) are handled by rules on existing edges combined with value-level UNKNOWN. Structural omissions ('rotating shaft has no support relationship', 'belt drive has no tensioning strategy') have no edge or value for a rule to evaluate. Value-level typing cannot flag a requirement that was never created. So a graph-plus-rules design with 0002's typing still reports nothing for omissions. Given the repo's default-pass patterns (1), the result becomes PASS or at most a warning. If an enrichment step like (3) runs first, a plausible link is invented and the omission disappears.

ARCHITECTURAL PROPOSAL (not a fact, not validated):
- ComponentType and PatternRole declare RequiredPort: {port_id, interface_type, role, cardinality, condition, satisfaction_alternatives, rule_provenance}.
  - condition example: applies only when motion=rotating.
  - satisfaction_alternatives example: 'two radial supports' OR 'one moment-capable support' OR 'host component provides internal support, with its load ratings as Facts that may be UNKNOWN'.
  - rule_provenance: STANDARD / HANDBOOK / OMNI_HEURISTIC etc.
- An InterfaceInstance binds exactly two ports, and every binding must be explicit (a user, Vega's proposal or pattern instantiation). Name or keyword similarity is never enough.
- An obligation closure pass creates one ObligationInstance per required port. Each gets PASS/WARN/FAIL/UNKNOWN plus rule_id, input fact_ids and provenance.
- An unbound required port is FAIL when its condition is known to hold, and UNKNOWN when the condition itself is unknown.
- A waiver is a separate record with provenance and a justification. It never deletes the obligation.
- Overall verdict: FAIL if any FAIL, else UNKNOWN if any UNKNOWN, else WARN if any WARN, else PASS. An empty obligation set gives UNKNOWN. PASS requires count(PASS or justified WARN) == count(obligations).
- Compatibility rules run per bound InterfaceInstance, using 0002-style Facts.
- InterfaceType owns per-side CAD feature templates (e.g., for shaft_to_bearing: a seat on the shaft side, a bore on the housing side, retention features conditional on role).
- CadObligations come only from bound instances whose compatibility verdict is not FAIL. Oli never gets geometry for an unbound or undecided port.
- Change to the mission's proposed flow: add an 'obligation closure' stage between 'interface graph' and 'compatibility analysis'.

EVIDENCE THAT COULD SUPPORT OR WEAKEN THIS (the Novelty Rule asks for this; not an experiment proposal):
- Supporting: take the mission's five patterns and remove one required relationship at a time. An edge-rule engine plus Fact typing emits no FAIL/UNKNOWN for those removals, while port closure flags each one.
- Weakening: Fact-typed required slots on records (e.g., shaft.radial_support_refs: Fact[list[ComponentId]] defaulting to UNKNOWN) catch every seeded omission, including context-dependent ones like fixed/floating, without a separate closure stage. In that case this hypothesis collapses into 0002.

Informal FrontierResearchScore (not authoritative): alignment 5, impact 5, information gain 4, generalizability 5 (ports and closure carry over to seals, springs, pneumatic fittings, electrical connectors, fixtures), novelty 3, experimentability 5 (seeded omissions on pure-Python fixtures, no CAD needed), risk 1, implementation cost 2.

claim: The decisive safeguard is an independently preserved assembly requirement contract, not closure over component ports. Component-derived closure can report PASS after an entire required subsystem disappears, because its obligations disappear with it. A requirement-driven evaluator can detect structural omissions without materializing a separate port-closure stage.
mechanism:
COMPETING EXPLANATION: The underlying failure is letting the candidate design define the scope of its own validation. Enumerating obligations from that same candidate makes coverage explicit but does not establish that the obligation set is complete. This differs from replacing ports with Fact-typed component slots: both remain vulnerable when their owning component or pattern instance disappears.

CONCRETE COUNTEREXAMPLE: A frozen mission requires independently identifiable outputs A and B. Both initially have component assemblies whose local support and interface obligations pass. Delete B's entire assembly and pattern instance while retaining A. Component-derived closure still has a nonempty, fully satisfied obligation set and therefore returns PASS. A separately preserved requirement for B remains unsatisfied. Checking only empty obligation sets cannot catch this partial deletion. Pattern roles solve it only if an independently retained contract requires that pattern or its function; that adds the competing mechanism.

ARCHITECTURAL ALTERNATIVE: Preserve a versioned AssemblyContract separately from the candidate graph: requirement_id, functional endpoints, operating_case_id, predicate_id/version, applicability facts, provenance, and declared completeness scope. Evaluate deterministic predicates directly over typed component and relationship records. Predicates may quantify over nodes, absent relationships, or paths; they need not run only on existing edges. Return a witness or counterexample with input fact IDs and graph/contract revisions. Component ports remain useful for interface typing, but are not the authority for validation coverage. A small v0.1 can use explicit Python predicates without a general constraint solver.

SEMANTICS: Missing representation is UNKNOWN when the relevant inventory or relationship scope is incomplete; absence is FAIL when the requirement applies and that scope is explicitly complete. A known applicability condition alone does not establish completeness. UNKNOWN and FAIL both prevent a validated handoff, while remaining distinct findings. Unsupported predicates also yield UNKNOWN. An empty check set cannot establish assembly validity, but an explicitly inapplicable interface category should not itself force the entire assembly to UNKNOWN.

MISSION EXAMPLES: Both designs can detect a missing support, tensioning strategy, retention relationship, or selected leadscrew support arrangement when the relevant component/pattern remains represented and the governing rule is supplied. A direct graph predicate can detect an absent edge; the limitation belongs to edge-only dispatch, not graphs generally. Component-derived closure can miss removal of the entire owning subsystem. The independent contract catches that removal, but still misses requirements omitted from the contract itself. Neither design establishes physical adequacy merely by finding relationships.

CAD BOUNDARY: Preserve unresolved CAD requirements as symbolic records with unresolved participants and evidence dependencies; release executable geometry only when the relevant prerequisites are satisfied. The proposal's 'compatibility verdict is not FAIL' includes UNKNOWN, conflicting with its prohibition on geometry for undecided ports. Also, a binary shaft-to-bearing interface cannot directly own a housing-side bore without an additional bearing-to-housing relationship or a multi-participant pattern.

claim: I accept Codex's central counterexample. If obligations are derived only from the candidate's own components and patterns, deleting a whole subsystem gives a false PASS, so my original claim is refuted for that fault class. I also withdraw the claim that a separate, materialized closure stage is necessary. Direct predicates that quantify over nodes can detect absent relationships. The counter-hypothesis still overreaches, though. A requirement contract that stays solution-independent cannot name the obligations a candidate introduces by its own choices. Examples are a belt tensioner, or a housing bore that exists only because the design chose bearings. So a contract-only evaluator must either miss those omissions or false-FAIL a valid alternative design. Revised claim: fail-closed completeness needs two things together. (A) An externally anchored, predicate-bound requirement contract, which catches whole-subsystem deletion. (B) Type-conditioned induced obligations over whatever the candidate selected, which catch omissions in design-introduced subsystems. How the check is evaluated (materialized obligations vs direct predicates) should change only coverage accounting, not verdicts. I propose a frozen, pre-registered 7-arm ablation on synthetic fixtures to separate these effects.
mechanism:
CONCESSIONS (from checking the lines Codex cited):
C1. Whole-subsystem deletion: accepted. Obligations derived from the candidate vanish with it. My hypothesis (a)-(c) is refuted for this fault class. This is a logical refutation, not yet an empirical one.
C2. My line "every validator has a default-pass shape" contradicts my own evidence. gates.py:37-39 returns BLOCKED when the gate list is empty. Narrowed to: several validators default to pass.
C3. "Graph rules cannot see missing relationships" holds only for rules dispatched per existing edge. reviewer.py:68-90 iterates over nodes and detects absent links.
C4. CAD gating: "compatibility not FAIL" wrongly let UNKNOWN through. Corrected rule: executable CAD obligations are emitted only when the interface and all prerequisite interfaces are PASS, or WARN with a recorded waiver. Otherwise the system emits a symbolic PendingCadObligation listing unresolved participants and fact dependencies.
C5. The housing bore does not belong to shaft_to_bearing. A bearing type declares two ports: inner_race (shaft_to_bearing) and outer_race (bearing_to_housing). Each InterfaceType owns the CAD templates for each of its sides.
C6. I accept completeness-scoped semantics, with one refinement. Completeness is declared per relationship category (support, retention, tensioning...) and carries provenance. If no declaration exists, absence is UNKNOWN. Handoff to Oli requires every category touched by the obligation set to be declared complete. That way, labeling scope 'incomplete' forever can never reach a validated handoff.

NEW REPO FACT (this turn): OMNI already stores requirements separately from the design, and they catch nothing. mission_graph Requirement (schemas.py:19-23) is free text copied from isy.validation_items (builder.py:262-276) with status defaulting to "unverified". Grep finds no code in mission_graph that ever sets it to verified or failed. reviewer.py never mentions requirements. validators.py:105-114 flags only an empty requirement list, at severity "info". backend/app has no requirement_id, acceptance_criteria or functional_requirements structure. Inference: storing an anchor is necessary but not sufficient. Each requirement needs a machine-evaluable predicate, a traceability binding, and provenance for the text-to-predicate translation. That translation is where fabricated knowledge would enter.

WHY A CONTRACT ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH (argument, to be tested): take the mission 'drive output B at a specified speed'. Candidate 1 chooses a belt drive and candidate 2 a geared output, and both are valid. If the contract's predicates stay solution-independent, nothing in the contract requires a tensioner, so removing it is a false PASS. If the contract adds 'belt drive requires tensioning', candidate 2 is false-FAILed, or the predicate is really a type-conditioned rule over candidate-selected types. That second case is mechanism (B) under another name. Frozen classification rule: a predicate counts as INDUCED if its quantifier domain is component or interface types chosen by the candidate and not named by the mission. Otherwise it counts as CONTRACT.

PROPOSED EXPERIMENT (bounded; pure-Python stdlib; synthetic; no CAD; no real tolerances or manufacturer data; all synthetic rules tagged OMNI_HEURISTIC/SYNTHETIC)
Arms:
- A0: repo-pattern baseline. Rules dispatched per edge, default PASS.
- Requirement source × evaluation strategy:
  - S1 induced-only, S2 contract-only, S3 contract + induced;
  - each run with E1 (materialized ObligationInstances, then graded) and E2 (direct predicates that return a witness or counterexample).
- Total: A0 + 6 arms = 7.
Fixtures: a frozen manifest with SHA-256, where every case carries an oracle label signed by a human.
Controls (oracle PASS):
- V1: two outputs. A is motor→coupling→shaft→2 bearings→housing. B is a belt drive with a tensioner.
- V2: same mission, but B is a geared output (tests substitution).
- V3: leadscrew stage with fixed and floating supports.
Single mutations:
- F1: remove one shaft_to_bearing on A (FAIL).
- F2: delete B's whole chain and its pattern instance (FAIL).
- F3: remove B's tensioner (FAIL; design-induced).
- F4: remove bearing_to_housing while shaft_to_bearing remains (FAIL; no executable housing-bore CAD may be emitted).
- F5: F1 with the support category declared incomplete (UNKNOWN).
- F6: shaft motion applicability UNKNOWN and support binding missing (UNKNOWN).
- F7: run a mission_graph-style gap-filler (bind to the first housing, like enrichment.py:99-116) before evaluation. Oracle FAIL: bindings without admissible provenance must be ignored.
- F8a: symbolic bore token ≠ seat token (FAIL).
- F8b: speed rating absent (UNKNOWN).
- F9: F3 plus a USER_PROVIDED waiver (WARN; obligation kept on record).
- F10: B deleted AND B missing from the contract. Expected to false-PASS in every arm; recorded as a residual blind spot, not scored.
Metrics (per arm):
- false PASS (primary), false FAIL, UNKNOWN on cases whose oracle is PASS or FAIL;
- requirement/rule-to-finding coverage, with provenance;
- CAD leakage: executable CAD emitted for unbound, UNKNOWN or FAIL interfaces;
- verdict identity between E1 and E2 for the same source.
Degeneracy guard: an arm that returns anything other than PASS on V1-V3 is disqualified. This blocks always-UNKNOWN wins.
Pre-registered predictions (mine):
- P1: S1 false-PASSes F2.
- P2: S2 false-PASSes F3 and F4, or false-FAILs V2.
- P3: only S3 gets 0 false PASS on F1-F9 and 0 false FAIL on V1-V3.
- P4: E1 and E2 give identical verdicts for every source. E2 reaches E1's coverage only by emitting one witness per quantified binding.
- P5: any arm without a provenance-admissibility check on bindings false-PASSes F7, whatever its source.
- P6: F10 false-PASSes everywhere.
Refutes me:
- S2 reaches 0 false PASS on F3/F4 with 0 false FAIL on V2, using only predicates classified CONTRACT; or
- S3 is not strictly better than S2 on false PASS; or
- E1 and E2 verdicts diverge.
Supports Codex over me: the first bullet, or S1 with any retained anchor matching S3.

The claim that a contract alone is not enough rests on the INDUCED/CONTRACT classification rule. If Codex's contract is allowed to hold generic type-conditioned predicates, S2 and S3 may merge and part of the disagreement becomes terminology. Its real content would then be where induced rules live and what provenance they carry.
Synthetic fixtures risk being tautological, because the implementers know the fault taxonomy. Hold-out mutations authored after the arms are frozen reduce this but do not remove it.

Oracle labels encode OMNI_HEURISTIC engineering judgments, such as 'a belt drive requires a tensioning strategy' and 'a leadscrew needs fixed/floating support'. Whatever verdict the experiment reaches, those are not validated engineering facts. Satisfaction alternatives (motor-internal bearings, fixed-center belts, self-aligning supports) are not covered in v1 of the fixture set.
Per-category completeness declarations could become a rubber stamp. The experiment tests the declared-vs-undeclared semantics but not whether declarations are honest.

P4 (E1 and E2 give identical verdicts) could fail for incidental implementation reasons rather than architectural ones. A divergence would need per-case diagnosis before being counted as a refutation.
The false-FAIL rate of type-conditioned induced rules across real, diverse designs is unmeasured. Small synthetic fixtures cannot show whether findings would become so numerous that they get ignored.
F10 shows that every arm stays blind to requirements missing from the contract. How Echo, or a human, makes the contract complete remains open and is outside this experiment.

claim: I accept the classification confound. My INDUCED/CONTRACT split depended on whether the mission text named a type, so S2's predicted loss was built into the design. I withdraw P2 and P3 as claims about architecture. Where predicates are stored no longer carries the disagreement. Under equal information, a unified contract and a split contract-plus-catalog design should be extensionally equivalent, so comparing them mostly tests implementation conformance. What actually decides fail-closed behavior is predicate kind and three-valued combination semantics, not storage. There are two kinds. (i) Existential anchors over mission endpoints. (ii) Universally quantified conditional rules held in a versioned type catalog. Both are independent of the candidate. My seq-1 error was deriving obligations from candidate instances instead of from anchors plus the catalog. OMNI already uses this shape outside mechanics: TestCube's arbiter takes required_check_ids from policy and also appends every observed check. I also report two new semantic hazards that the current fixture list cannot detect. First, reusing a worst-of lattice (gates.py-style max) for satisfaction alternatives either false-FAILs valid alternative designs or releases designs with no admissible strategy. Second, where completeness declarations live changes the oracle label for whole-subsystem deletion (FAIL vs UNKNOWN). I propose a revised experiment built around these hazards, plus metamorphic properties over exhaustively generated single deletions. That avoids needing a blinding custodian.

K2. Unified vs split with identical predicates, facts and policies: I agree equivalence is the expected result. Because that expectation is close to tautological, I demote the comparison to an implementation-conformance check. It is not a distinguishing arm.
K3. Oracle repairs 1-5: accepted. Frozen policies are below.
K4. Metrics: accepted. Full 4x4 confusion matrix, release decision, finding identity, applicability outcome, evidence dependencies and CAD release. For direct evaluation, a coverage record is required for every root predicate, including empty domains.

The inline comment gives the reason: "An extra regression failure must not disappear because only focused tests were required." A required check that is missing yields passed=False with reason MISSING_CHECK.
- That is anchors (external) plus observed checks, combined without letting either set shrink the other.
- It governs CI checks, not mechanics. It shows the pattern fits OMNI's architecture; it does not show the pattern is mechanically adequate.

NEW HAZARD H1: satisfaction alternatives need a disjunction operator
- reliability/gates.py:6-11,37-41 offers exactly one combinator: max over PASS<WARN<FAIL<BLOCKED. There is no disjunction. I did not survey other modules for one.
- Satisfaction alternatives are an OR: two radial supports OR one moment-capable support; adjustable tensioner OR fixed-center strategy.
- Hand evaluation, ordering FAIL>UNKNOWN>WARN>PASS for AND and best-of for OR. This is NOT an observed run; the in-memory pilot was not executed, see evidence.
  - V4, valid fixed-center with no tensioner. Tensioner alternative absent in complete scope gives FAIL; fixed-center alternative gives PASS. Worst-of gives FAIL, a false FAIL. Best-of gives PASS.
  - F3b, tensioner absent and fixed-center fact UNKNOWN. Worst-of gives FAIL, a wrong label. Best-of gives UNKNOWN.
- Encoding the alternatives as separate optional rules avoids those false FAILs, but then nothing fires when no strategy exists (F3a), which releases the design.
- Prediction: without a distinct OR combinator, an implementation must fail either V4 or F3a.

NEW HAZARD H2: completeness location changes the F2 label
- Codex's repair 5 scopes completeness per assembly scope and revision. If B's subassembly owns its completeness declaration, deleting B also deletes the declaration. Anchor B then yields UNKNOWN, not FAIL.
- Both outcomes block release, so safety holds. The oracle label still differs, and an arm could be scored wrong for a correct result.
- Frozen rule: anchors are evaluated against completeness declared on the assembly-revision record held with the contract. Subassembly declarations govern only L rules inside that subassembly.
- Split F2 into F2a (revision-level declaration present: FAIL) and F2b (only subassembly-owned declarations, deleted with B: UNKNOWN, non-release).
- Property of this rule: deleting any completeness declaration can move FAIL to UNKNOWN, never to PASS.

NEW HAZARD H3: empty quantifier domains
- Folding an empty domain with AND gives UNKNOWN (or PASS under a default-pass fold). Neither is right.
- Frozen rule: the root-predicate coverage record is NOT_APPLICABLE when the domain is empty AND the type inventory for that scope is declared complete. It is UNKNOWN when the inventory is incomplete, because an unrecorded belt drive could exist.
- NOT_APPLICABLE is excluded from aggregation but counted in coverage. If no applicable records exist at all, the result is UNKNOWN.
- V2 (geared output, no belt drive) tests this.

FROZEN POLICIES (proposal; all rules tagged OMNI_HEURISTIC + SYNTHETIC; no real tolerances or manufacturer data)
- SYN-SUPPORT-001: for each shaft with motion=rotating, satisfy (at least 2 radial_support bindings) OR (1 moment_capable_support binding) OR (host_internal_support, whose load-rating facts may be UNKNOWN). The motion fact UNKNOWN makes applicability UNKNOWN.
- SYN-TENSION-001: for each belt_drive, satisfy adjustable_tensioner binding OR fixed_center_strategy fact.
- SYN-HOUSING-001: for each bearing, outer_race requires a bearing_to_housing binding. Executable housing-bore CAD is released only if that binding is PASS.
- SYN-VALUE-001: bore token must equal seat token; mismatch gives FAIL, a missing token gives UNKNOWN.
- Absence semantics: an unsatisfied applicable requirement gives FAIL if its scope is complete, otherwise UNKNOWN.
- Provenance admissibility (paired control, the same in every arm): a binding whose provenance is not in the admissible set is treated as absent when checking satisfaction. It also emits a separate finding of kind PROVENANCE_POLICY (release-blocking). The mechanical verdict then follows absence semantics. The two findings keep distinct IDs.
- Waiver v0 record: waiver_id, finding_id, assembly_revision_id, rule_id@version, authority_role, justification, provenance.
  - Eligible only for a raw FAIL caused by absence, where the catalog marks the rule waivable. Never eligible for value FAILs, PROVENANCE_POLICY findings, or facts CAD geometry depends on.
  - A USER_PROVIDED source is not authority by itself; authority_role must be a human engineering sign-off role.
  - The raw verdict is kept; the disposition becomes WARN_WAIVED.
  - The waiver is invalidated by any change to assembly_revision_id. It never releases CAD whose participants are unresolved.
- CAD release: executable only when the interface and all prerequisite interfaces are PASS, or WARN_WAIVED with no unresolved participants. Otherwise a symbolic PendingCadObligation is emitted.

claim: The coverage/storage confound is resolved, but the revised experiment still has a vacuous mutation property and incomplete quantifier semantics. Repair those before verification; an explicit AND/OR tree is a reasonable proposal, not an experimentally established necessity.
mechanism:
H1: I accept that conjunction over unchanged alternative verdicts cannot implement disjunction. However, excluding 'disjunction encoded somewhere' makes the refutation criterion true by definition. A deterministic predicate that counts admissible satisfaction witnesses can implement alternatives without a general AND/OR schema. Compare explicit trees against such predicates as conformance alternatives, not expressive impossibility. Keep raw satisfaction in {true, false, unknown}; WARN and WARN_WAIVED are dispositions, not additional truth values. Freeze how dispositions affect release separately.

H2/H3: Independently retained, revision-bound completeness is useful, but its location alone does not establish coverage. Freeze its quantified scope and category. More importantly, H3 handles only EMPTY incomplete inventories. Counterexample: the recorded inventory contains one belt drive with a valid strategy, but the type inventory is incomplete. Every observed instance passes, yet an unrecorded belt drive may fail. The universal root must remain UNKNOWN. Conversely, an existential endpoint anchor with an admissible witness can PASS despite an incomplete inventory. A missing existential witness yields FAIL only with complete scope; otherwise UNKNOWN. For a universal root, a decisive observed counterexample yields FAIL, while all observed instances passing requires domain completeness to establish PASS. Treat complete empty universal domains as covered/inapplicable, without suppressing mandatory existential anchors. Add these paired cases explicitly.

MP1 IS VACUOUS UNDER THE PROPOSED GENERATOR: V1–V4 are releasing controls. Comparing each control with a single deletion never exercises the antecedent 'non-release before mutation.' An always-releasing implementation therefore satisfies MP1 on that generated set. Start information-loss transitions from non-releasing F cases too, or enumerate comparable pairs of partial-information states. Freeze the contract, catalog, candidate identities, and waiver policy; replace evidence values with UNKNOWN while retaining their required slots. Distinguish information withdrawal from correction or deletion of a design choice. This gives a meaningful property without repeatedly adding carve-outs.

MISSING DISTINGUISHING CONTROL: Test two cases with the same alternative verdicts {PASS, FAIL}. In one, FAIL means an unselected satisfaction strategy is unavailable, so the requirement passes. In the other, a valid strategy exists but an installed interface has a known incompatibility, so its independent integrity obligation still blocks release. A naive best-of implementation can hide that second defect. This tests obligation scoping, which both implementations could misunderstand identically.

OTHER PREDICTIONS: Q5 is too strong: choosing the first region is invariant under consistent ID/name renaming and may pass MP2. Add record-order permutation and a requirement that changing names/order cannot create an admissible binding. Q7 is also unsupported: omitting NOT_APPLICABLE coverage can leave V2's aggregate verdict unchanged while losing coverage evidence. Score coverage separately. Demoting unified-versus-split storage to conformance loses no decisive information here.

FREEZE GAP: The listed catalog does not yet specify the speed predicate used by F8b, the leadscrew obligations exercised by V3, the actual provenance admissible set, or which rules are waivable for F9. These omissions prevent independent implementations from sharing a genuinely frozen oracle.
